thread:
nora: Quick report: the Go generator sample leaks goroutines when a caller cancels using ctx. Repro in sample: start generator, cancel after first token, pprof shows leftover goroutine in handshakeLoop waiting on ackCh.

ben: repro'd it. minimal snippet I used:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
iter := client.Generator(ctx, req)
go func() { time.Sleep(30*time.Millisecond); cancel() }()
for iter.Next() { _ = iter.Token() }
log.Println("err:", iter.Err())
```
Leftover goroutine is in generator.go:handshakeLoop.

ashwin: likely handshake reader doesn't select on ctx.Done() or ackCh is never closed on early cancel. Two quick options: make iterator implement io.Closer and show defer iter.Close() in samples, or fix runtime to auto-clean on ctx.Done().

mira: we should do both: ergonomic ForEach helper for quickstarts, plus make Close automatic on ctx cancel. Samples should show ForEach and the manual pattern with defer Close.

ben: plan: add a small watcher goroutine when creating iterator that calls an idempotent cleanup (sync.Once) closing ackCh, implement io.Closer, and add ForEach(ctx, fn) with signature func(ctx, Token) error. I'll draft a PR with unit tests verifying ackCh closed once and an integration that cancels mid-stream and asserts goroutine count returns to baseline.

dev-bot: Created issue #371: "go-sdk: generator handshake goroutine leak on ctx cancel" https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/issues/371. Milestone: v0.14.2.

nora: thanks. once PR lands update sample app and onboarding docs. tagging ashwin to audit Dedicated runtime paths so we don't miss mirrored code.

ashwin: will audit. sound plan.
